title: Higher-Order Continuation Semantics

basis.scope: Introduce higher-order continuation structure in which continuations themselves become admissible operands for lawful construction, transformation, and composition while preserving the bounded semantics of the RT Calculus.

core_rule.statement: Higher-order continuation semantics apply only after EVAL_024 and only to explicit continuation operands that satisfy higher-order admissibility; Lift(C) may embed a first-order continuation into the higher-order domain; lawful continuation transformations preserve typing and process equivalence where defined; higher-order continuations remain bounded, preserve the existing reduction kernel, and RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Introduce higher-order continuations in which continuations themselves become admissible operands for lawful construction, transformation, and composition while preserving the bounded semantics of the RT Calculus.

canonical_claims.statement: Higher-order continuations are explicit only; continuation operands must be declared.
Continuation lifting embeds a first-order continuation into the higher-order domain without changing RT_core.
Higher-order transformations preserve typing and process equivalence where defined.
Higher-order continuations remain subject to REDUCE_025 and bounded admissibility.

formal_objects.name: Higher-Order Continuation
formal_objects.definition: A continuation whose operands may themselves be continuation objects.

formal_objects.name: Continuation Transformation
formal_objects.definition: A lawful transformation operating on continuation objects while preserving admissibility.

formal_objects.name: Continuation Lift
formal_objects.definition: The operation that embeds a first-order continuation into the higher-order continuation domain.

formal_objects.name: Higher-Order Continuation Class
formal_objects.definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to higher-order admissibility.

requirements: Transformation preserves process equivalence where defined

relationships.recursive_continuation: Rec(C) may participate as an operand within HC(C).
relationships.reduction: Higher-order continuations reduce using existing reduction semantics.

admissibility_rules: Continuation operands must remain well formed.
Higher-order transformations shall preserve process equivalence where defined.
Higher-order continuations remain subject to REDUCE_025.
Recursive continuations remain governed by GuardRec(C).
invariants: Higher-order semantics introduce no new primitive.
